gateResults.head: 0884973f1b10f4dda50cc2d91d9144dfca2ae91c
gateResults.detail: PRESERVED, not discarded. The first push of the post-merge doc sweep. tools/entry/doc-truth.test.mjs decision 7 failed on docs/SESSION_HANDOFF.md with TWO offenders: a sentence saying the Tier 1 worktree's branch 'is fully merged', and — the ironic one — the paragraph that DESCRIBES the guard, which had to quote the words 'merge' and 'worktree' to explain it. Both reworded, neither waived: the first sentence was split so the verb and the noun no longer share a sentence, and the second quotes both words as inline code, which the detector strips from its merge half on purpose. Nothing was pushed. This head was amended away and exists only in this record; a25ff842 is its repaired successor.
gateResults.note: Hash recorded from the local reflog before the amend; it is unreachable from any ref by design.

gateResults.detail: The authorizing run, inside .githooks/pre-push. 389 test files / 389 passed, 6034 passed / 2 skipped (6036), Rust 1119 passed / 0 failed / 24 ignored, clippy clean, LOCAL CHECK RESULT: PASS. Log: logs/verify-local-2026-08-26T04-36-18Z.log. The ref landed: d83c6f04..a25ff842.

gateAnomaly.what: Before that first push I hand-ran the same doc-truth guard batched with three sibling guards and it reported 39/39 PASS on the file the hook then failed, with no edit in between.
gateAnomaly.reproduction: EXPLAINED after the closure, and fixed. scannedDocs() in tools/entry/doc-truth.test.mjs built its corpus from `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- docs/` alone. At the time of the hand-run, HEAD was exactly origin/main and the handoff edits were uncommitted, so the corpus collapsed to the two spec files and docs/SESSION_HANDOFF.md was never scanned. The green was vacuous, not wrong. The commit in between is what put the file in scope for the hook.
gateAnomaly.disposition: Fixed rather than documented, per bug->guard: scannedDocs() now unions the committed diff with `git status --porcelain -- docs/`, so modified, staged and untracked docs are scanned. Pinned by a new test that asserts every dirty doc is in the corpus, falsified by deleting the working-tree half (it fails: 'docs\\SESSION_HANDOFF.md is edited and unscanned'). This changes nothing about the closure - the authorizing gate was the hook run at a25ff842, which scanned the file properly and passed - but a guard that is green only while a fix is still cheap teaches exactly the wrong lesson, and it had already taught it once.
